## Role and Cost Boundary

This page owns transport from the fabrication yard, foundation installation, topside installation, offshore hookup and offshore commissioning. Platform fabrication and converter electrical equipment are costed elsewhere.

| Physical scope | Treatment | Cost owner |
|---|---|---|
| Load-out and transport | Included here | **This page** |
| Jacket or foundation installation | Included here | **This page** |
| Topside lift or float-over | Included here | **This page** |
| Offshore hookup and commissioning | Included here | **This page** |
| Platform fabrication | Excluded | [HVDC and Substation Platforms](../platforms/hvdc_and_substation_platforms.qmd) |
| Converter equipment and onshore station | Excluded | [HVDC Converter Stations](../electrical_infra/hvdc_converter_stations.qmd) |

<span class="cost-owned">Green = booked on this page</span>
<span class="cost-reference">Grey = reference only; not booked on this page</span>

## Available Cost Evidence

The internal model description uses 750 EUR/kW for “platform and installation” [@internalModelDescription2026]. That value combines platform fabrication, transport and installation, so it cannot be adopted as installation cost alone.

The DEA offshore-station coefficient also includes the platform and station installation within a broader offshore-station value [@danishEnergyAgency2025Transport]. It does not publish a separate heavy-lift or hookup share.

| Cost-stack element | Reference value | Status | Cost owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Legacy platform + installation allocation | <span class="cost-reference">750 EUR/kW</span> | Combined scope; context only | This page and [Platform](../platforms/hvdc_and_substation_platforms.qmd) |
| Platform fabrication | <span class="cost-reference">TBD</span> | Costed separately | [HVDC and Substation Platforms](../platforms/hvdc_and_substation_platforms.qmd) |
| Adopted platform-installation CAPEX | <span class="cost-owned">TBD</span> | Requires vessel and schedule basis | **This page** |

No portion of the 750 EUR/kW combined allocation is booked until a defensible split is available.

## Bottom-Up Cost Model

A future installation estimate should use:

$$
C_\mathrm{platform\ installation}
=
C_\mathrm{mobilisation}
+\sum_v r_v t_v
+C_\mathrm{port}
+C_\mathrm{hookup}
+C_\mathrm{commissioning},
$$

where $r_v$ and $t_v$ are the rate and required duration for each vessel or marine spread.

The schedule should distinguish:

- foundation transport and installation;
- topside load-out and transport;
- heavy-lift or float-over operations;
- weather contingency;
- cable and auxiliary-system pull-ins;
- offshore hookup; and
- testing and commissioning.

## Principal Cost Drivers

| Driver | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Topside and foundation mass | Determines vessel class, transport method and lift feasibility |
| Water depth and soil | Governs foundation and piling scope |
| Distance to fabrication yard and port | Drives transport and support-vessel time |
| Lift strategy | A single heavy lift and modular lifts require different fleets and schedules |
| Weather window | Controls waiting time and schedule risk |
| Offshore commissioning duration | Determines accommodation and support-vessel requirements |

## Architecture Applicability

This category applies to the offshore electricity-export platform and any centralised-hydrogen platform. The required vessel spread must be recalculated for each architecture rather than transferring the HVDC allocation unchanged.
